subject: Failover playbook and comparative test plan for StratusHealth evaluation
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: failure-mode tests & comparison matrix we discussed

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can move the evaluation forward: 

Summary of what we heard from StratusHealth:
- Primary concern: predictable behavior during partial outages (single-region/network blips) and graceful degradation under heavy burst traffic.
- Secondary: per-route rate limits and token-level cost sensitivity for high-throughput batch jobs.
- Procurement: standard SLA + audit artifacts required for vendor review.

What Redwood proposes for the bakeoff (high level):
1) Failover & routing tests — simulate a region-level outage and validate automatic failover to a compatible model variant in another region; measure RTO and error surface.
2) Error-budget burn scenarios — sustained 5–10% elevated error rate to observe throttling/fallback behavior and alerting.
3) Tail-latency stress — 95th/99th/99.9th latency under mixed small/long-context requests.
4) Rate-limit & throttling behavior — confirm per-token and per-request enforcement and what graceful backoff looks like for your SDKs.
5) Cost/perf comparison — head-to-head vs Stratus’ current hyperscaler endpoints (you mentioned AWS SageMaker + Google Vertex in the call). We will include dedicated-capacity and hosted API modes in the matrix.

Proposed owners & timeline:
- Redwood runbook & test harness: Marissa (cc) — we will deliver a runnable test plan by Wed 12/02.
- Stratus test dataset & access account: Alex / procurement — please confirm by Fri 12/04.
- Requested outcome: pass/fail criteria per test + numeric SLO measurements so you can present to your ops team.

Attachments: I attached the initial failover playbook draft (redwood-failover-playbook.md) and a short SLO worksheet to capture acceptable thresholds (stratus-required-slos.xlsx).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the contact for the test account and whether test traffic can be routed to a temporary CNAME we provide?
- Do you have any absolute must-haves for the SLA (e.g., 4 nines vs 3 nines) or specific audit artifacts beyond SOC2 (certificates, retention policies)?

I’ll sync with Marissa to finalize the test plan once you confirm.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@stratushealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stratushealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: failure-mode tests & comparison matrix we discussed

Diego — thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- We can stand up a test account scoped to non-prod data. Procurement will need a statement of work + expected ingestion volumes for their review (looping them in).
- For the bakeoff, the two hyperscaler endpoints we want compared are:
  * AWS SageMaker Endpoints (multi-AZ deployment)
  * Google Vertex AI Prediction (regional)

- SLA expectation: we need to demonstrate >= 99.95% observed availability over a 30-day window for production, but for the evaluation a 7-day window with test traffic that demonstrates behavior under failover will suffice.

Questions: 
1) Can Redwood provide a short list of the specific metrics we should collect on our side (e.g., per-request jitter, token counts, upstream error codes)?
2) Will the test harness include synthetic region outages or do we run the failover from our side?

Procurement note: please send the SOW sample and an initial estimate of monthly committed spend for dedicated capacity — we will need that to get legal engaged.

— Alex
Alex Monroe
Director, Product Integrations — StratusHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@stratushealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: failure-mode tests & comparison matrix we discussed

Alex — adding the technical test matrix. I also attached a runnable harness we use internally (redwood-failover-playbook.md) that includes the scripts we run for: 

- simulated AZ/regional network partitions (failure injection),
- progressive traffic ramp to exercise burst/backpressure logic, and
- long-context tail-latency tests (1k/2k token ranges).

Minimum metrics we recommend you capture: 
- request_id, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, total_tokens_out, model_variant, response_status (2xx/4xx/5xx), upstream_http_code, region_served, retry_count, cache_hit (prefix or KV), and observed_cost_tokens.

SLOs we will aim to show in the bakeoff (baseline proposals — we can tune with your ops team):
- Availability: 99.95% (measured at 1m granularity, 30d window)
- Error rate: <= 0.05% (5e-4) for production traffic patterns
- 95th/99th/99.9th latency targets: dependent on model and sequence length; we will provide profiles per-model in the test report.

Failover behavior we will validate: 
- Automatic routing to a pinned compatible model variant in a secondary region with observable RTO <= 30s for control-plane handover and token streaming resumption within 60s.
- Transparent limited-capacity fallback: if dedicated capacity saturates, Redwood can redirect to a lower-cost model variant preserving response shape (we'll measure output divergence in the report).

For the hyperscaler comparison: we will run identical request workloads against your SageMaker/Vertex endpoints and Redwood (hosted API + a dedicated pool) and produce a side-by-side of: cost-per-token, tail latency, observed error budget burn, and failover recovery time.

I'll schedule a short technical sync (30 min) for Wednesday 12/03 to align on the dataset and credentials. Diego — can you confirm a time?

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@stratushealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: failure-mode tests & comparison matrix we discussed

Alex / team — great, thanks. Confirming the plan and a few admin items: 

- Technical sync: Wednesday 2026-12-03 at 10:00 PT (Marissa will lead). Marissa: please share the Meet link and the test harness repo before the call.
- Procurement: Diego attaching a one-page SOW summary and a provisional cost range for a 6-month dedicated pool commitment (estimate only). If procurement confirms, we can push an initial PO to Legal for a standard enterprise contract.
- DocuSign / access: I will send the temporary access instructions and a DocuSign demo agreement after the technical sync.

Immediate asks from Stratus: confirm the test account contact and whether you can expose a test CNAME or accept our client to call your test endpoints. If either is constrained we can host all traffic to a Redwood-managed test account and share logs.

Thanks again — we want this to be low-friction and measurable so your ops and procurement teams can compare apples-to-apples.

Links: https://hub.redwood.ai/deals/RDW-STR-2026-0912

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
